newsitem.title: USA: Georgia governor urges speedup in welfare changes.
newsitem.headline: Georgia governor urges speedup in welfare changes.

text.p: Georgia Gov. Zell Miller has proposed moving up the start date by six months for a plan to limit welfare benefits to four years, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said Wednesday.
The changes were due to take effect at the beginning of fiscal 1998 on July 1. Miller's proposal would retroactively move up the start date to Jan. 1.
The governor said the changes were urgently needed to "change a (welfare) spending system that has been on autopilot for too long."
Miller also proposed a $12 million reserve fund to make sure welfare payments are covered if applications increase during economic downturns.
Lawmakers will debate the proposals over the next few weeks as part of the supplemental budget allocations.
